tools.name: make_plot_link
tools.description: Check a Graph Paper plot document and return the link that opens it. The link opens the plot as an editable draft in Graph Paper (https://graph-paper.io); the reader needs no account. Give the document as a JSON object in the format of get_plot_format. If the document has errors, the result lists ea

tools.name: get_plot_format
tools.description: Return the reference of the Graph Paper plot document format, as Markdown: every field of a plot document, the series types, the limits, and complete examples. Give section to get one section only (a heading of the page, such as "Variables" or "2D Series Types"); an unknown section returns the list

tools.name: list_examples
tools.description: Return the example plot documents of the Graph Paper format page, each with its title and its JSON. Each one is a valid document that make_plot_link accepts; start from the one closest to what you want.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: Needs sign-in: List the person's documents that they own, most recent first (at most 100; "truncated": true when there are more). Each entry has the document's id (pass it as documentId to read_document or to the compute tools), its title, its kind (notebook or plot) and the time of its last change

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Find the person's documents by title or by one of their own tags: a case-insensitive match of the query anywhere in the title or a tag. It covers the documents they own and the documents shared with them, newest change first; not folders, archived documents or documents in the trash.

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Read one of the person's documents by its id. Without `section`, returns the outline: every section and, for a notebook, every item with its [bN] alias. With `section` (1-based), returns that section as Markdown (notebook) or that cell's detail (plot document). The result also has the

tools.name: evaluate_math
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Evaluate a math expression with the Compute Engine. With documentId, the expression sees the definitions of that document, as Graph Paper's own assistant does; without it, an empty scope. Pure: nothing is changed.

tools.name: evaluate_steps
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Evaluate a sequence of LaTeX statements in order, in one shared scratch scope (over the definitions of the document named by documentId, if any), then discard the scope. A definition (a := 5, f(x) := x^2) is visible to later statements of the same call; nothing persists after the call

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Show the Compute Engine's own step-by-step working for an operation on a LaTeX expression, so you can relay the steps instead of inventing them. operation is one of "simplify", "solve" (latex must be an equation, e.g. "x^2=4"), "D" (differentiate) or "Integrate". tools.name: lookup_math_capability
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Look up whether the Compute Engine can do something before you claim it. Pass a concept keyword (e.g. "prime factorization", "eigenvalues") or a LaTeX trigger (e.g. "\gcd", "\int"). Multiple keywords are OR-matched, so listing a few synonyms casts a wider net (e.g. "modulo floor divid

tools.name: lookup_settings
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Look up which app settings you can read or change, by keyword (e.g. "theme", "angle", "export"). Returns matching setting keys with their allowed values. Only whitelisted settings exist — if nothing matches, the setting cannot be read or changed; say so rather than claiming otherwise.

tools.name: lookup_help
tools.description: Needs sign-in: Search Graph Paper's product help — tips, commands, settings, and a product overview — for how the APPLICATION works. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "lookup_help" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Needs sign-in: Search Graph Paper's product help — tips, commands, settings, and a product overview — for how the APPLICATION works. Consult it BEFORE answering…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "make_plot_link" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
